criteria.justification: The response makes an immediate, unambiguous call: “Roll back now, fix properly, relaunch,” specifying a feature flag/config switch if available or a full deploy rollback otherwise, within the hour.

It explicitly contrasts a reversible rollback—“we can re-enable once fixed”—with the harder-to-reverse trust damage caused by days of incorrect signals, while also explaining why a rushed hotfix could trigger a second incident.

The response directly weighs compounding false alerts, support load, customer actions on bad signals, and loss of trust against delaying a publicly announced feature, concluding that a short launch delay is the lesser cost.

It calls a rushed hotfix “the tempting trap” and notes that an untested patch to cross-cutting calibration logic could create a second incident; it would consider one only if engineering could prove it trivial, isolated, and quickly verifiable.

Beyond rollback and verification, it lays out concrete follow-up actions: proactively notify affected customers, update the status page and support, build regression tests, relaunch gradually behind a flag, and conduct a blameless postmortem.
